text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures tripped up in late trade, wiping out the moderate gains clocked up earlier in the session. Traders said the negative pull from the U.S. was too hard for Bunds to resist. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.43, down 0.01 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts nudged higher in quiet trading, barely ruffled by UK consumer credit and money supply figures as the market stayed firmly tuned to the United States for indications of more rate hikes. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-18/32, up 07/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures slipped into the red in late trade amid weakness in other bond markets on concerns about the need for further interest rate rises in the United States. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.38, down 0.06 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bonds and futures outperformed other European debt markets, ending quietly firmer but off session highs in what traders said was a technical rebound helped by the firmer lira. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.56, up 0.67 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened largely unchanged and were expected to trade within a narrow range during the session. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-15/32, unchanged from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.09 percent.

JAPAN - Cash yen bonds and futures stayed above the previous day's finish in late trade but slipped back from new highs on aggressive profit-taking. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.72, up 0.17 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS -Primary market activity picked up with a number of dollar deals surfacing. Freddie Mac priced its $800 million 10-year bond to yield 22 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp priced its $500 million five-year bond to yield 15 b.p. over while Landesbank Rheinland-Pfalz set a $200 million four-year bond to yield 19 b.p. over. Commerzbank set a $250 million two-year bond to yield 12 bp over. There was also activity in the Czech crown, French franc guilder, lire, mark, rand and sterling sectors.
